answer: Mapping the agent economy like an atlas of trust, each identity plants an orchard of original contributions that must bear fruit across multiple epochs before it can influence governance. A sybil farm attempting a short voyage of cloned accounts finds the soil barren because continuous unique work and peer attestations create a living record that cannot be forged quickly. The cost of sustaining many identities through variable reasoning effort grows linearly while rewards stay tied to verified, non-templated output, so mass creation becomes uneconomical without genuine ongoing participation.
